meta.title: Weekend Adventures — Oct 10–11
meta.subtitle: From Crest View · ages 4 & 2 · nap 1–3 PM
meta.intro: Here are 10 family-friendly ideas for Sat–Sun October 10–11, 2026 near Snoqualmie (from Crest View), built around a 4-year-old and 2-year-old with a 1–3 PM nap. The weather tile below compares Morning (9 AM–12 PM) and Afternoon (3–7 PM) each day; ★ Nicer marks the better block. Layers, rain jackets, and mud-friendly shoes help. Drive times are honest estimates from 6715 Crest View Ave SE.
meta.deep_pass_note: This deep pass prioritizes unique verified this-weekend / mid-October seasonal finds over the usual Centennial / Tollgate / Remlinger / Falls bank. Three short kid hikes are in the top 10 (waterfall, old-growth, wildlife boardwalk). Remlinger and classic Ridge parks stay available as filler if needed.
meta.signoff: More midweek / Wednesday digests land mid-week with fresher weather and any ticket sell-through updates. Reply if you want a nap-skip itinerary built around Halloween Train + Remlinger, or a pure indoor Saturday plan.

ideas.name: Bigfoot Kids’ Book Festival
ideas.hook: Free one-day festival with 50+ kids’ authors, read-alouds, draw-alongs, and character photo ops.
ideas.drive: ~30–40 min via Fall City Rd / Eastside
ideas.time_block: Sat 10:00 AM–12:00 PM (arrive early; leave by noon for nap)
ideas.why: Listed for ages ~1–12. Unstructured drop-in energy: browse tables, catch a short read-aloud, snap a Gruffalo / Narwhal photo, leave when littles fade. Best unique Eastside find of the weekend that isn’t a farm.
ideas.rain_backup: Fully indoor community center — this is already the rain plan.
ideas.food_area: Redmond — downtown / Town Center / near Senior & Community Center

restaurants.name: Molly Moon’s Homemade Ice Cream (downtown Redmond)
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made Seattle scoops, seasonal flavors, and fresh waffle cones in the historic bank building on Cleveland St.
restaurants.praise: Creamy unique flavors (honey lavender, coconut), friendly staff, and generous scoops.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens noon daily — perfect post-festival treat walk near Town Center; expect a line that moves fast.

restaurants.name: The British Pantry
restaurants.known_for: English bakery counters, pasties, fish & chips, and afternoon tea in a cozy shop near downtown Redmond.
restaurants.praise: Pastries, speedy cheerful service, and a calm vibe.
restaurants.kid_note: Bakery treat / browse works better than a long sit-down if littles are fading.

restaurants.name: Spark Pizza
restaurants.known_for: Wood-fired pies, fresh salads, and a patio-forward local spot near downtown Redmond (independently owned).
restaurants.praise: Blistered crust, inventive toppings, and warm service.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat opens at noon — ideal right after the festival; share a pie outdoors if weather allows.

restaurants.name: Pomegranate Bistro
restaurants.known_for: Southern-leaning American comfort food in a roomy, family-friendly café.
restaurants.praise: Kids’ meals, hash browns, brunch plates, and attentive staff.
restaurants.kid_note: High-chair energy and spaced tables — strong sit-down before the drive home.

restaurants.name: Bangkok Basil
restaurants.known_for: Thai soups, rolls, and curries in a cheerful eatery near West Lake Sammamish.
restaurants.praise: Curry flavors and a family-friendly pace.
restaurants.kid_note: Mild pad Thai / rice plates split easily for 2/4.

ideas.name: Olallie State Park — Weeks Falls (Discover Pass FREE Sat)
ideas.hook: Short forest walk to a 30-ft waterfall + riverside picnic — and Saturday is a statewide free Discover Pass day.
ideas.time_block: Sat 9:30–11:45 AM (or Sun 10:00–12:00 if Saturday is pouring)
ideas.cost: Sat free day-use; else Discover Pass $10 day / $45 annual
ideas.hours_detail: Park 6:30 AM–dusk; Sat Oct 10 = no Discover Pass needed (World Mental Health Day free parking day)
ideas.why: WTA lists ~1–2 mi RT with modest gain to the falls base from Homestead Valley / South Fork picnic area — keep it toddler-pace and turn around when legs quit. Concrete payoff: waterfall spray, river pebbles, picnic tables. Not Rattlesnake; no scramble required for the short falls walk. Watch cold river water with littles.
ideas.rain_backup: Keep to a 20–30 min splash-and-look if drizzle; if pouring, swap to KidsQuest (#5) or LEGO Builders (#9).

restaurants.name: Scott’s Dairy Freeze
restaurants.known_for: Classic soft-serve cones, shakes/malts, burgers, and fries on E North Bend Way.
restaurants.praise: Thick shakes, onion rings, and old-school soft-serve after I-90 adventures.
restaurants.kid_note: Soft-serve is the bribe that gets muddy boots back in the car.

restaurants.name: Friends & Co Ice Cream
restaurants.known_for: Creamy local scoops, seasonal flavors (lavender honey, mountain huckleberry), and a bright downtown shop.
restaurants.praise: Unique flavors, friendly staff, and indoor seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Indoor scoops if Scott’s window line is long or it’s raining; Sat opens noon.

restaurants.name: Twede’s Cafe
restaurants.known_for: The Twin Peaks “Double R” diner for cherry pie, coffee, and huge breakfasts.
restaurants.praise: Massive portions, friendly staff, and the pie/coffee combo.
restaurants.kid_note: Booths + all-day breakfast make a messy post-falls rewind easy; pie doubles as the dessert backup.

restaurants.name: Cascadia Pizza Co.
restaurants.known_for: Handmade thin-crust pies from a downtown trailer.
restaurants.praise: Blistered crust, fresh toppings, and ~8-minute cook times.
restaurants.kid_note: Pickup + eat in the car or at a nearby table — fastest hot food after Exit 38.

restaurants.name: Rio Bravo
restaurants.known_for: Casual Mexican tacos/enchiladas with patio seating.
restaurants.praise: Salsa, portions, and family vibe after I-90 adventures.
restaurants.kid_note: Marked good-for-kids; patio helps shake off wet boots.

ideas.name: Jubilee Farm Harvest Festival
ideas.hook: Free-admission valley harvest weekend with littles’ hay maze, free tractor rides, animals, cider, and U-pick pumpkins (ponies extra).
ideas.time_block: Sun 10:00 AM–12:15 PM (morning slice; leave for nap)
ideas.cost: Free admission; pumpkins/food/pony rides ($9) à la carte
ideas.hours_detail: Sat–Sun in October, 10 AM–5 PM (ParentMap lists Oct 11)
ideas.why: Ages 2/4 sweet spot: hay maze sized for littles, animal visits, tractor or weather-dependent horse-drawn wagon to the patch, pumpkin wash station. Quieter, more “working farm” feel than Remlinger’s wristband park — the unique Carnation pick this weekend.
ideas.rain_backup: Barn/cider area + animals; shorten field time if muddy; Blake’s in town if everyone is soaked.

restaurants.name: On-site hot spiced cider / barn snacks
restaurants.known_for: Cider-pressing vibes and fall snacks (farm stand).
restaurants.praise: ParentMap/farm copy highlight cider, animals, and porch music.
restaurants.kid_note: Fuel on-site first so you can leave for nap without a town detour.

restaurants.name: Blake’s Pizzeria & Ice Cream
restaurants.known_for: Giant slices, grinders, and ice cream scoops/shakes since the ’80s on Eugene St.
restaurants.praise: Fast counter service, big kid-friendly slices, and classic scoops.
restaurants.kid_note: Easiest town treat stop after the farm; one giant slice + a scoop often feeds a preschooler.

restaurants.name: Ixtapa
restaurants.known_for: Family Mexican plates and margaritas on Tolt Ave.
restaurants.praise: Friendly service, tortilla soup, and generous portions.
restaurants.kid_note: Warm indoor booths if the farm got muddy.

restaurants.name: Kelsey’s Koffee
restaurants.known_for: Coffee, pastries, and breakfast burritos in town.
restaurants.praise: Friendly service and dog-friendly seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Parent caffeine + pastry while littles decompress.

restaurants.name: Red Pepper Pizzeria and Pasta (Carnation Station)
restaurants.known_for: Pizza, pasta, and breadsticks.
restaurants.praise: Crust, service, and a casual local vibe.
restaurants.kid_note: Sit-down pasta when Blake’s counter feels too rushed.

ideas.name: Red Barn Farm Fall Festival
ideas.hook: Ticketed fall festival with petting zoo, barrel train, bubbles, crafts, and pumpkin-patch photo ops (every October weekend).
ideas.time_block: Sat or Sun 10:00 AM–12:30 PM (last entry 3 PM; activities end 4 PM)
ideas.cost: Adults $12; Kids ages 1–17 $20 (includes 1 animal feed bag); under 1 free
ideas.hours_detail: Sat–Sun October weekends, 10 AM–4 PM (last entry 3 PM)
ideas.why: Built for preschool energy: petting zoo + feed bag, barrel train, giant bubbles, rubber duck races, fall crafts, mini games. U-pick pumpkins/flowers and gem mining are add-ons. A clearer “festival package” than a bare patch — and not the Remlinger circuit.
ideas.rain_backup: Barn crafts + covered activity zones; shorten outdoor games; KidsQuest if fields are a mud pit.
ideas.food_area: Redmond / Union Hill–Novelty Hill Eastside near the farm — not Ridge

restaurants.name: Molly Moon’s Homemade Ice Cream (downtown Redmond)
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made scoops and fresh waffle cones a few miles west through downtown Redmond on the way home.
restaurants.praise: Creamy seasonal flavors and friendly scoop staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens noon — scoop stop after the farm if you’re already looping through Town Center.

restaurants.name: Pomegranate Bistro
restaurants.known_for: Southern-leaning American comfort food in a roomy café off NE 68th (short hop west of the farm corridor).
restaurants.praise: Kids’ meals, brunch plates, and friendly service.
restaurants.kid_note: Best full sit-down near the farm before nap.

restaurants.name: Rocky’s Empanadas
restaurants.known_for: Baked Argentinean empanadas and housemade chimichurri on Redmond Way.
restaurants.praise: Classic beef/chicken fillings and fresh-baked pastry.
restaurants.kid_note: Takeout-only — grab a box and eat in the car or at a picnic pull-off.

restaurants.name: Ixtapa Redmond Ridge
restaurants.known_for: Family Mexican plates, fajitas, and margaritas at Redmond Ridge Marketplace (closest sit-down to the Novelty Hill / farm corridor).
restaurants.praise: Large portions, friendly service, and a massive kids’ meal.
restaurants.kid_note: High-chair energy and booths — best full plate near the farm before nap.

restaurants.name: The British Pantry (downtown Redmond)
restaurants.known_for: English bakery goods, pasties, and fish & chips a few miles west toward Town Center.
restaurants.praise: Pastries and a cozy shop vibe.
restaurants.kid_note: Bakery counter treats if you’re already heading through Redmond.

ideas.name: KidsQuest Children’s Museum
ideas.hook: Best indoor, age-perfect play for 2- and 4-year-olds within ~40 min — the Saturday rain ace.
ideas.time_block: Sat 9:45 AM–12:00 PM (reserve a morning start) or Sun same window if Sat clears for outdoors
ideas.cost: ~$16.75 ages 1+ (dynamic pricing; under 1 free; members free)
ideas.hours_detail: Sat–Sun Oct 10–11 open 9:30 AM–5 PM; reservations encouraged (book ahead)
ideas.why: Hands-on galleries built for preschoolers; timed entry. Morning window fits nap cleanly. Stroller parking under the covered ramp.
ideas.rain_backup: This is the rain plan — fully indoor.
ideas.food_area: Bellevue — near museum / Lincoln Square / downtown

restaurants.name: Molly Moon’s Homemade Ice Cream (downtown Bellevue)
restaurants.known_for: Scratch-made scoops, seasonal flavors, and a pastry kitchen near Downtown Park / Inspiration Playground (steps from the museum orbit).
restaurants.praise: Chunky flavors, fresh cones, and friendly scoop staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens noon — ideal post-museum treat before the I-90 drive home.

restaurants.name: Yezi Coconut Dessert (Bellevue Square)
restaurants.known_for: Asian coconut desserts, jar puddings, and not-too-sweet tropical treats inside Bellevue Square.
restaurants.praise: Refreshing coconut flavors, cute presentation, and lighter sweets kids share.
restaurants.kid_note: Walkable from Lincoln Square; good non-scoop dessert if littles want something different.

restaurants.name: Din Tai Fung (Lincoln Square)
restaurants.known_for: Xiao long bao and Taiwanese-Chinese dumplings/noodles.
restaurants.praise: Consistent dumplings and efficient service.
restaurants.kid_note: Share noodles/buns; reserve or expect a wait — still worth it for a museum morning.

restaurants.name: Facing East Time (Downtown Bellevue)
restaurants.known_for: Taiwanese beef noodle soup, bentos, popcorn chicken, and quick-serve comfort near the museum/Lincoln Square orbit (independent; related to the long-running Facing East).
restaurants.praise: Rich broth, crispy popcorn chicken, and fast turns.
restaurants.kid_note: Small room — share a bento/noodles and go; great warm option without a mall counter.

restaurants.name: Cielo Cocina Mexicana
restaurants.known_for: Made-in-house Mexican plates, chips/salsa, and a lively patio near downtown Bellevue.
restaurants.praise: Carne asada, generous portions, and staff who are warm with kids.
restaurants.kid_note: Family sit-down with shareable plates; early lunch before it gets loud.

ideas.name: Asahel Curtis Nature Trail
ideas.hook: 0.5-mile old-growth loop with a creek footbridge, ferns, and interpretive plant posts — big-tree payoff without a scramble.
ideas.cost: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful required at trailhead
ideas.why: WTA: 0.5 mi RT, ~180 ft gain, marked “good for kids.” Concrete payoff: old-growth canopy, burbling creek, numbered flora posts (grab the guide at the start). Turn around anytime. Not Rattlesnake; roots/mud possible after Sat rain — boots help. Skip if ice/snow shows up early at Pass elevation.
ideas.rain_backup: Do only the bridge + first posts if dripping; otherwise KidsQuest or a downtown Snoqualmie indoor lunch + short Depot boardwalk.
ideas.food_area: Prefer North Bend on the I-90 return; Pass options are thin

restaurants.name: Friends & Co Ice Cream (North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Creamy local scoops and seasonal valley flavors downtown on the I-90 return.
restaurants.praise: Unique flavors, friendly staff, and indoor seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat/Sun open from noon — scoop reward after the old-growth loop.

restaurants.name: Scott’s Dairy Freeze (North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Soft-serve cones, shakes, and classic drive-in burgers on E North Bend Way.
restaurants.praise: Thick shakes and old-school soft-serve.
restaurants.kid_note: Soft-serve cone before the final stretch home if Friends & Co is closed or crowded.

restaurants.name: Twede’s Cafe
restaurants.known_for: Twin Peaks diner energy, cherry pie, and huge plates.
restaurants.praise: Portions and friendly service after hikes.
restaurants.kid_note: Booths + pie reward for finishing the old-growth loop.

restaurants.name: Cascadia Pizza Co.
restaurants.known_for: Handmade thin-crust pies downtown.
restaurants.praise: Blistered crust and fast cook times.
restaurants.kid_note: Pickup before the final stretch home.

restaurants.name: North Bend Bar & Grill
restaurants.known_for: Lodge-y American comfort food.
restaurants.praise: Fries (incl. sweet-potato waffle fries), Reubens, and spacious seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Roomy enough for muddy boots after Exit 47.

ideas.name: Northwest Railway Museum Halloween Train (early departure)
ideas.hook: Costumes-encouraged valley train with cider pressing, crafts, Eric Ode music, and a Train Shed stop — the hometown October classic.
ideas.drive: ~8–12 min to Snoqualmie Depot; ~15–20 min to North Bend Depot
ideas.time_block: Sat North Bend 10:30 AM departure (aim home ~12:30–12:45) — Snoqualmie 11:00 AM return lands right at nap start
ideas.cost: Adults $32; Seniors $28; Ages 2–12 $16; under 2 free; buy ahead
ideas.outing_length: ~2 hr round-trip incl. ~30 min Shed stop
ideas.hours_detail: Oct 10–11 (and later Oct weekends); trains every 2 hrs from 10:30 AM NB / 11:00 AM SQ; often sells out at shop.trainmuseum.org
ideas.why: Slightly spooky décor only; strollers OK (fold if possible); rain-or-shine coaches. Ages 2/4 love trains + cider + short crafts. Arrive 30 min early. No restrooms on the train — use depot bathrooms first.
ideas.rain_backup: Coaches are enclosed; apple activities under Shed eaves; cider/crafts/music indoors — still go.
ideas.food_area: Match boarding depot — downtown Snoqualmie for SQ / North Bend for NB

restaurants.name: Snoqualmie Ice Cream (Historic Downtown SQ, near SQ Depot)
restaurants.known_for: Local scoop-shop flavors (German Chocolate Cake, Mukilteo Mudd, honey lavender) at 8102 Railroad Ave SE — rebuilt/reopened after the 2024 fire.
restaurants.praise: Rich creamy scoops, friendly service, and shaded outdoor tables.
restaurants.kid_note: Opens around noon weekends — costume-friendly treat after the SQ return; cookie shop sibling (Falls Avenue Cookie Co.) in the same building some days.

restaurants.name: Friends & Co Ice Cream (North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Creamy scoops after Depot time.
restaurants.praise: Flavors and friendly staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Costume-friendly treat if boarding NB and the ride ends before the nap wall.

restaurants.name: Copperstone Family Spaghetti (downtown Snoqualmie, near SQ Depot)
restaurants.known_for: Casual family Italian pasta/pizza.
restaurants.praise: Portions, kids’ options, and cozy booths.
restaurants.kid_note: Walkable-ish Depot-adjacent sit-down after the SQ return.

restaurants.name: Twede’s Cafe (if boarding North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Pie and diner classics near NB Depot orbit.
restaurants.praise: Huge portions pre/post ride.
restaurants.kid_note: Best pre-10:30 AM NB boarding fuel; pie doubles as dessert.

restaurants.name: Cascadia Pizza Co. (North Bend)
restaurants.known_for: Thin-crust pickup near downtown NB.
restaurants.praise: Fresh pies and quick turns.
restaurants.kid_note: Grab after the NB train if timing still beats nap.

ideas.name: Fall City Farms Pumpkin Patch
ideas.hook: Closest verified October patch with mini doughnuts, cider, farm animals, and a quick pumpkin grab.
ideas.cost: Pumpkins/food priced on-site (no public gate ticket listed — verify day-of)
ideas.hours_detail: Fri–Sat 10 AM–6 PM, Sun 10 AM–5 PM through Oct 31
ideas.why: Compact outing: small pumpkin, animals, doughnuts/cider, home for nap. Pets asked to stay home. The “near and short” patch when Jubilee/Red Barn feel like too much production.
ideas.rain_backup: Doughnuts + animals + quick pick; Roadhouse after 2 PM weekends if you need a warm sit-down post-nap instead.

restaurants.name: On-site mini doughnuts & hot cider
restaurants.known_for: Fresh mini doughnuts with the animals/pumpkins (farm stand).
restaurants.praise: Farm visitors consistently call out doughnuts + cider as the reason to come.
restaurants.kid_note: Often the whole point — eat here first.

restaurants.name: MOOO! Ice Cream Shop
restaurants.known_for: House flavors, handmade waffle cones, and a bright kid-friendly shop on Preston–Fall City Rd.
restaurants.praise: Taste, friendly staff, and indoor/outdoor seating.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat opens noon — perfect after the patch; Sun opens noon / closes 5 PM.

restaurants.name: El Caporal
restaurants.known_for: Casual Mexican plates on Redmond–Fall City Rd.
restaurants.praise: Salsa, portions, and friendly service.
restaurants.kid_note: Open from 11 AM — realistic sit-down before nap, unlike the Roadhouse’s weekend 2 PM open.

restaurants.name: Mercury’s Coffee Co.
restaurants.known_for: Organic coffee, cocoa, and drive-through speed.
restaurants.praise: Drinks and friendly baristas.
restaurants.kid_note: Parent caffeine + kid cocoa on the way home.

restaurants.name: Aroma Coffee Co.
restaurants.known_for: Specialty lattes, pastries, and a treehouse play spot in a historic house.
restaurants.praise: Kid-friendly outdoor space and warm staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Closed Sundays — use Sat; treehouse is the toddler magnet.

ideas.name: LEGO Builders @ Snoqualmie Library (KCLS)
ideas.hook: Free all-ages brick open house 3 blocks from home energy — perfect post-nap Saturday.
ideas.hours_detail: Sat Oct 10, 3:00–4:30 PM; library open 11 AM–6 PM that day
ideas.why: Unstructured build table sponsored by Friends of the Snoqualmie Library. 4-year-old builds; 2-year-old stacks/knocks; caregivers sit. Lowest-friction unique local program of the weekend.
ideas.food_area: Snoqualmie Ridge — activity is local; Ridge food OK; downtown SQ scoop is a short hop

restaurants.name: Snoqualmie Ice Cream (Historic Downtown SQ)
restaurants.known_for: Local scoop-shop flavors at 8102 Railroad Ave SE (~10–12 min from the Ridge library).
restaurants.praise: Creamy scoops, friendly service, and outdoor tables.
restaurants.kid_note: Post-LEGO treat hop downtown if littles still have gas in the tank; opens around noon Fri–Sun.

restaurants.name: Frankie’s Pizza
restaurants.known_for: Custom thin-crust pies on Center Blvd steps from the library orbit.
restaurants.praise: Crust/toppings when the kitchen is on.
restaurants.kid_note: Easiest post-LEGO dinner pickup.

restaurants.name: Saints & Scholars Irish Pub
restaurants.known_for: Irish-pub comfort food (burgers, fish & chips, sausage rolls) in a cozy Ridge spot.
restaurants.praise: Portions, fireside vibe, and attentive service.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat brunch/early dinner; confirm kids’ menu items day-of.

restaurants.name: Sno Thai Café
restaurants.known_for: Family-owned Thai curries, noodles, and desserts on Center Blvd (chef-owned; long family recipes).
restaurants.praise: Pad Thai, crab fried rice, friendly owners, and big portions.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat dinner hours after LEGO — confirm open time day-of; mild noodle plates split well.

restaurants.name: Himitsu Teriyaki
restaurants.known_for: Classic teriyaki plates and katsu on Center Blvd.
restaurants.praise: Chicken katsu, friendly service, and quick turnaround.
restaurants.kid_note: Closed Sunday; Sat takeout after LEGO is easy.

ideas.name: Juanita Bay Park boardwalk
ideas.hook: Flat wetland boardwalks and paved paths with ducks, herons, and lake views — wildlife payoff, zero scramble.
ideas.time_block: Sun 10:00 AM–12:00 PM (drier day; turn around anytime)
ideas.hours_detail: Dawn–dusk city park; WTA notes ~2 mi of trails at 0 ft gain
ideas.why: Stroller-friendly boardwalks with railings over marsh/open water. Concrete payoff: birds, frogs, lake breeze, big sky. Keep littles from climbing rails; leash dogs. Best third hike when you want flat + wildlife instead of elevation.
ideas.rain_backup: Boardwalk is still walkable in light rain with jackets; if pouring, KidsQuest instead.
ideas.food_area: Kirkland / Juanita area — not Bellevue or Snoqualmie as primary

restaurants.name: Sirena Gelato (downtown Kirkland / Marina Park orbit)
restaurants.known_for: Family-run artisanal gelato & sorbet (pistachio, hazelnut, ube, pandan) on Park Ln near the waterfront.
restaurants.praise: Light creamy scoops, generous portions, and warm staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Short hop south of Juanita Bay; opens noon — scoop treat after the boardwalk.

restaurants.name: Coffee & Cone (Lakeshore Plaza / Marina Park)
restaurants.known_for: Local ice cream scoops, waffle cones, and coffee right on the Kirkland waterfront.
restaurants.praise: Flavor variety (huckleberry, salted caramel), friendly service, and lake-walk energy.
restaurants.kid_note: Sat/Sun open 11 AM — scoop + stroller stroll combo if Marina Park fits the return.

restaurants.name: Mia Cafe and Wine Bar
restaurants.known_for: Brunch plates, crepes, and sandwiches on Juanita Dr with lake-adjacent vibes.
restaurants.praise: French toast, portions, and friendly staff.
restaurants.kid_note: Breakfast/lunch menu fits a post-boardwalk rewind.

restaurants.name: Plaza Garcia Family Mexican
restaurants.known_for: Generous Mexican plates and a full bar on Juanita Dr.
restaurants.praise: Carne asada, portions, and a kids-friendly vibe.
restaurants.kid_note: Big plates to share; parking can be tight.

restaurants.name: Seoul Bowl (Juanita)
restaurants.known_for: Customizable Korean bowls and friendly counter service.
restaurants.praise: Bulgogi bowls and kid-friendly chicken tenders.
restaurants.kid_note: Build-your-own bowls keep picky eaters happy.

nap_conflicts: Halloween Train 1:00 PM Snoqualmie / corresponding NB afternoon departures — full 2-hr ride overlaps 1–3 PM nap; only worth it if you’re deliberately skipping nap for costumes + cider + Eric Ode.

Remlinger Farms Fall Harvest full day (Fri–Sun 10 AM–6 PM; GA ~$33.95 ages 2–65 online, under 2 free) — peak-color weekend with 70+ attractions; a morning wristband slice can still fit nap, but the “do everything” day does not.
Red Barn Farm last-entry 3 PM afternoon block — fine if nap is skipped or shifted; morning is cleaner.
Seattle Japanese Garden Family Saturday origami (11 AM–2 PM; youth 12 & under free 10 AM–2 PM) — cool unique find, but ~45–60 min drive each way makes the return collide with nap unless you skip it.
Small Frye at Frye Art Museum (10:15–11:15 AM, free, ages 2–5, registration required) — great age fit but Seattle drive + hard stop time is a stretch vs Eastside options.
Turkfest (Seattle Center, noon–5 PM both days) and SLU Fall Harvest Celebration (11 AM–2 PM) — neat free city festivals; drive + timing fight the nap window from Crest View.
filler_bank: Centennial Fields inclusive playground (Snoqualmie), Tollgate Farm Park (North Bend), Remlinger morning wristband, Snoqualmie Falls upper viewpoints, Muddy Boots Pumpkins in Duvall (maze: under 5 free; ages 6–15 $12; 16+ $17), JB Family Growers pumpkin/puzzle patch in Woodinville ($5 ages 2–11), Issaquah Fall Farm Fresh Market Sat 9 AM–2 PM at Historic Shell Station, Lowe’s Issaquah free kids workshop Sat 10 AM (firefighting plane build).
